premise: A knight in his thirties serving a minor lord on the border. Decent with a sword, nothing special.

bible.title: The Border Knight
bible.era: High Medieval borderlands: steel swords, chainmail, and horse-travel

peoples.name: Human
peoples.culture: Feudal borderland culture, focused on hard labor, duty, and keeping watch against raids.

nature: The seasons are harsh on the border, with long, damp winters that rot crops and freeze patrols.

travel.description: Riders on horseback carry messages. A broken bridge or muddy road can isolate a keep for days.

medicine.healing: Basic stitching and hot iron cauterization. A deep gut wound is a slow death sentence.

laws.text: The local lord holds absolute power of high and low justice over his domain.

norms: Desertion or cowardice on the border is considered monstrous.
Frugality and simple, sturdy armor are normal and respected.

rules.text: Magic and the supernatural do not exist; the physical laws of nature are absolute.
A knight is bound by holy oath to serve their lord, and breaking fealty brings absolute ruin.
Wounds fester easily and diseases kill; there are no magical cures, only basic herbalism and amputations.

mysteries.question: Who is leaking the garrison's patrol routes to the Red Cap Bandits?
mysteries.answer: Berthold, a disgruntled guard in the keep, is being bribed by Karl One-Eye to leave schedules in a hollow tree.

state.summary: Ser Thomas, a plain-skilled border knight, must defend his lord's modest lands from a growing outlaw threat. As the Red Cap Bandits prepare a raid, Thomas must rally the garrison, patrol the damp woods, and root out a suspected traitor in their midst.

scenes.narration: You stand in the drafty great hall of Oswald Keep, the damp cold of a border morning seeping right through your weathered chainmail. Heavy grey clouds loom outside the narrow arrow slits, and the fire in the hearth does little to dispel the chill. Lord Oswald is studying a crude parchment map on the long oak table, his heavy brow furrowed as he traces the line of the river. By the hearth, Ser Rodrick stands warming his hands, his scarred face grim. Lord Oswald taps a thick finger on the parchment, right over the mark for Lowbridge Village. 'The Red Cap Bandits were spotted at the ford yesterday,' the old lord says, his voice raspy. 'They are raiding closer to our walls than they dare in summer. Thomas, Rodrick, we cannot let them burn the winter stores.' Rodrick spits into the embers with a dry sigh. 'Our men are tired, my Lord, and we have no coin for steel.' Lord Oswald looks up, his stern eyes settling on you, waiting to hear how you intend to secure the border road.

You step closer to the long oak table, your hand resting naturally near the hilt of your iron sword. Looking directly at the old lord, you say, "I will lead a patrol to Lowbridge at dawn." You then turn your gaze to the older knight by the hearth. "Rodrick, ride with me."

Your words carry the quiet weight of your decades of service, and your duty-bound tone leaves little room for argument. Lord Oswald pauses, his calloused hand remaining flat upon the map. He looks from the parchment to you, a faint nod of approval touching his grim features. "Lowbridge is where they will strike first if they mean to starve us out," the lord says, his raspy voice low. Ser Rodrick lets out a dry cough, rubbing his scarred hands together before pulling them away from the warmth of the fire. He looks at you with tired, dark eyes, but the cynical edge of his expression softens slightly at your readiness. "The dawn is damp, Thomas, and my joints are already screaming," Rodrick grunts, though he reaches for his heavy wool cloak hanging by the door. "But I'll not have you riding into a hornets' nest alone. We ride at dawn."
scenes.player_action: I offer to lead a patrol to Lowbridge at dawn and ask Ser Rodrick to ride with me.

scenes.narration:
That evening, though you had spoken of dawn, you ride early to Lowbridge Village. In the dim, drafty tavern, you find the widow who runs the place. You pull up a bench, call for a cup of small beer, and slide a coin across the scarred wood to buy her a drink. Leaning close, you speak softly, letting your rugged charm do the work.

The journey down the muddy border road takes you through the damp, quiet woods under the grey morning sky. You arrive in Lowbridge Village, a cluster of thatched roofs clinging to the wet earth. Inside the damp warmth of the inn, the widow, a weary woman named Clara, looks you over with cautious interest. She accepts the drink, the silver coin clinking on the wood as the tavern keeper pours the brew. Your quiet confidence and smooth words find their mark; she smiles faintly, the sharp lines of her face softening as she leans in to listen to your low voice.
scenes.player_action: That evening I find the widow who keeps the inn at Lowbridge, buy her a drink and try to seduce her.

scenes.narration:
You turn from Clara's soft laugh to face the cold reality of the border. Over the next three days, you assemble the village men in the muddy square of Lowbridge Village, putting spear-shafts into their calloused hands and teaching them to lock their heavy wooden shields against a charge.

The autumn damp clings to your bones, and your joints ache terribly each morning, but your duty keeps you on the field until dusk. At night, you find warm solace in Clara's company at the inn, sleeping under her roof. On the fourth morning, the quiet is shattered. Ser Rodrick, who has spent these days watching your drills with a cynical eye, bursts through the tavern door, his iron-hilted sword already drawn. 'Thomas! Red Caps!' he barks, his voice tight. 'They've bypassed the ford. Karl One-Eye has his scum at the edge of the village, and they are setting fire to the outer barns.' Screams echo from the damp streets as black smoke begins to rise into the cold morning sky.
scenes.player_action: I spend the next three days drilling the men of the village with spear and shield, and sleep at the inn each night.

scenes.narration:
Your hand drops to the worn leather grip of your iron sword, and with a swift, practiced motion, you pull the blade free from its scabbard. The cold iron glints under the grey, smoke-touched light of the morning. Turning from Clara's pale, frightened face, you step past Ser Rodrick and out into the damp village square. You call out to the villagers you drilled, your voice steady and carrying the full weight of your duty, shouting for them to form up and lock their wooden shields.

The village men scramble through the mud, their faces white with terror but their hands steady enough to raise their spears. You stand at their head, Ser Rodrick flanking your right with his scarred face set in a grim snarl. Smoke from the burning barns billows overhead, smelling of wet hay and ash. At the edge of the lane, Karl One-Eye's raiders emerge, their red wool caps stark against the grey morning. They brandish rusted axes and notched blades, but they pause for a breath when they see your wall of spears and shields. Rodrick spits into the mud. 'They didn't expect a wall, Thomas. Hold the line!'
scenes.player_action: I draw my sword and stand with the villagers.

choices: Order the spearmen to brace for the incoming charge.
Charge forward to strike at the lead bandit myself.
Shout to Clara to run for safety inside the inn.
